chunks: Whether you plead forgiveness for them or not, God will not forgive them, even though you plead seventy times, for they disbelieved in God and His Apostle; and God does not show transgressors the way.
ai.seo_question: Why does God say He will not forgive those who disbelieved even if the Prophet asks for them seventy times?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Istighfar) is often interpreted as establishing the principle of divine decree overriding prophetic intercession for those entrenched in hypocrisy (Munafiqun). The specific number 'seventy' is viewed by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as either a literal count or a symbolic representation of completeness, highlighting that their disbelief was absolute despite the Prophet's persistent pleas. This underscores the distinction between general mercy and specific forgiveness for the persistently transgressive.
